blocks.content: The Citizenship Act, 1955, prescribes three ways of losing citizenship whether acquired under the Act or prior to it under the Constitution: renunciation, termination and deprivation.

rows: Declaration made by an adult citizen giving up Indian citizenship.
Minor children lose Indian citizenship (can resume at age 18).
Voluntarily acquiring the citizenship of another nation.
No direct impact specified under this specific provision.
Obtaining citizenship by fraud, disloyalty to Constitution, or 7 years continuous stay abroad.
Does not automatically extend to minor children unless specified by order.

items: When a male or female person renounces Indian citizenship, every minor child of that person also loses citizenship, but can reclaim it upon turning 18.
Termination of citizenship does not apply during a war in which India is engaged, to prevent citizens from evading national duties.
Deprivation is mandatory if a naturalised/registered citizen is sentenced to imprisonment for not less than 2 years in any country within 5 years of registration/naturalisation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Citizenship Act of 1955 prescribes three distinct modes of losing Indian citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, and Deprivation.
Renunciation is a voluntary act by an Indian citizen of full age and capacity, which also leads to the loss of citizenship for their minor children.
Termination takes place automatically by operation of law when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country.
Deprivation is a compulsory termination of citizenship by the Central Government on grounds of fraud, disloyalty, unlawful trade during war, or prolonged absence abroad.
A minor child who lost Indian citizenship due to parental renunciation may resume Indian citizenship within one year of attaining full age.
